To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) a chromatographic column evaluation for GLSs profiling in cauliflower by means UHPLC-HRMS has been performed for the first time, (ii) a new chromatographic system, consisting of two Kinetex XB C18 columns, was developed for the analysis of this class of metabolites, (iii) a large number of GLSs, some of which never previously identified in cauliflower, were tentatively identified by means of UHPLC-MS/MS

the chromatographic system composed of Luna Omega Polar column, Kinetex XB-C18 column and Kinetex XB C18 column, with mobile phase A: 5mM ammonium bicarbonate, 0.1% formic acid and B: 5m M ammonium bicarbonate in acetonitrile, 0.05% formic acid, resulted to be the best for the analysis of cauliflower GLSs.

the untargeted approach is suitable for the characterization of complex phytochemical mixturs, and that a suitable chromatographic separation is a key step to achieve a good metabolite characterization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new approach to the chromatographic separation of GLSs, a class of highly polar metabolites, which is still challenging in chromatographic separation.
the evaluation of different RP stationary phases for GLSs separation and the development of an analytical method for the untargeting profiling of GLSs.
the development of an untargeted method for the analysis of glucosinolate in cauliflower.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the developed analytical method could be a valid alternative to the methods already present in literature.
the developed method could be used for the untargetted profiling of intact GLS in cauliflower, with the aim to identify and characterize GLSs in the sample.
, in the present case, the use of the Luna polar C18 column resulted to be the best compromise between GLSs separation and MS sensitivity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the untargeted analysis of intact GLs in cauliflower is a promising tool for the study of this important class of secondary metabolites.

, despite the availability of alternative chromatographic systems, the RP chromatographic approach could represent a valid choice for the analysis of complex matrices such as cauliflower extracts, thanks to the development of new stationary phases.

the untargeted GLSs profiling is an effective approach for the characterization and identification of these metabolites in complex biological samples, and that the use of a chromatographic system with a long and high resolution column, in the case of RP chromatography, can improve the results.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the chromatographic column choice is crucial for the analysis of complex biological mixtures.
the use of a single RP chromatographic column, such as Luna Polar, is a valid alternative to other separation techniques for the analysis of complex GLSs mixtures.
a careful selection of the chromatographic column is crucial for a successful analysis of complex biological mixtures.
